§C.12 The annotation QA checklist

Procedure

Work a table in this order, and run the same eight checks again before you call the page done.

1. Frame test first

Decide what belongs to the table by border and fill, then deal with the bands. → Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3

2. Count N from the leaf tracks

Take a body row and count the leaf columns — that is N. Then verify every header row's colspans sum to N, and that no group colspan covers the stub. → Multi-Row Header Tiers§9.3.3

3. Prove every rowspan

A repeated value printed once is a rowspan. Printed k times at distinct y-coordinates, it is k separate cells. When you cannot tell by eye, extract the word boxes. → Repeated Identical Values§9.5.4

4. Walk parallel blocks independently

Where the page repeats a structure — one block per year, one per topic — check each block has all of its sub-sections. It is easy to complete the first block carefully and skim the rest.

5. End-of-table check

The bottom edge is where content is most often lost. Check for:

  • the last printed row
  • trailing summary lines → Bottom Edge Totals and Islands§9.7.1
  • detached islands → Bottom Edge Totals and Islands§9.7.1
  • sparse trailing columns → Barely-Existing Columns and Headers§9.3.1

6. Record equivalences — don't resolve them silently

When a page genuinely admits two encodings, write the canonical form and record that the other reading is also defensible. → Accepted Alternatives§A.1

7. Keep claim types separate

Never blend these into one verdict. Say which one you mean:

what you can see on the page · what an existing annotation says · a choice you made between two defensible encodings · a settled convention · an open question

This is what stops you writing "the annotation is wrong" when what you actually observed is "the annotation differs from what I would have written".

8. Escalate conflicts

Do not silently choose among open options.

Where two conventions are both live, record both and flag the page. A silent pick becomes precedent.

The completion record

Before you call a page done, you should be able to answer:

  • Which image and which crop did you inspect?
  • Which case does this fall under?
  • What is directly visible on the page?
  • What is an encoding choice you made?
  • What settled convention, if any, makes that choice the canonical one?

One page can carry several independent issues — a phantom header row, a repeated value wrongly spanned, and an out-of-frame title can all sit in a single crop. Record them separately rather than giving the page one verdict.

Working a chart

Seven checks, in order, before a chart's rules are done:

1. Census the points

Count positions × series — plus printed callouts, plus every panel — before judging any value: that is the rule count full coverage owes. A skipped series, tail, or panel is the number-one coverage failure. On the judge families the census includes the judged facts — every whisker span, box, gantt mark, and unambiguous choropleth region owes its chart_judge_point (The Ground-Truth File§C.13). → Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1 · Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3

2. Check every label

Printed text only, copied whole, the minimal set that uniquely locates the point; unlabeled positions by their axis value; a title fragment only to break a tie between charts. No colors, no chart-type words, no appended units, no merged dimensions. → Labels§11.1.2

3. Sweep for printed values first

On the marks, beside slices, in the legend, at line ends, in the side text — before estimating anything. A printed value you missed becomes a wrong estimate; every printed value is exact and tolerance-free. → Values and Tolerances§11.1.4 · Legend and Overlay Values§11.2.4

4. Verify the estimated values

Visual center, read against the mark's own axis (watch second axes and log bands), stacks and steps as their own spans, tolerance from the readability buckets. → Values and Tolerances§11.1.4 · Dual-Axis and Combo Charts§11.2.2 · Stacked Bars and Waterfalls§11.2.9 · Log Scale Charts§11.2.6

5. Audit the zeros and the gaps

A baseline mark or an empty labeled position is 0; a point no label set can locate, or a whisker end, carries no rule — deliberately, not by omission. → Values and Tolerances§11.1.4 · Scatter and Error Bars§11.2.8

6. Hunt invented content

No rules for reference ink or event callouts, no invented label text, no computed values, no expanded abbreviations, no tolerance on printed values. → Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3 · Labels§11.1.2

7. Check the file

The envelope (expected_markdown null, test_rules, doc tags), one flat rule list, need_estimate tags on estimates, tool-managed fields untouched, ids appearing on save — not from you. → The Ground-Truth File§C.13

Before publishing a multi-page document

Checks that only fail when you look across pages, not at one — see Document Rules§4.1:

  • [ ] The document type and its cover were decided once, and every page follows them
  • [ ] Every recurring margin band is filed the same way on every page it appears on
  • [ ] No heading repeats on more than half the pages — one that does is furniture filed as structure
  • [ ] No page after the first opens at a top-level heading unless that page actually prints one
  • [ ] Every ⚖️ choice is encoded the same way on every page, and the page that made it is flagged
  • [ ] Every table that runs across a page break is one fragment per page, none is joined, and both fragments carry matching continuation flags

Before publishing a Block layout

A page-level layout pass has its own gate. Every line must be true:

  • [ ] Every meaningful visible region has one correct Block and class, or is explicitly ignored with a valid reason
  • [ ] Each Block's layout class matches the corresponding Markdown element's class in Elements§3.1; any disagreement was resolved against the printed page
  • [ ] Table and chart captions use <caption> inside their table HTML, first if read before the object and last if read after it; each retains its Caption class and its own box
  • [ ] Separate paragraphs, columns, list items, captions and notes are not merged together
  • [ ] Table and Picture boundaries contain the complete object without absorbing captions or nearby prose
  • [ ] Reading order is complete, contiguous and correct — starts at 0, no gaps, no duplicates
  • [ ] Imported and generated Block suggestions were reviewed individually
  • [ ] Hide boxes was used to sweep for gaps, clipping, duplicates and wrong classes
  • [ ] The Block annotation is marked Checked
  • [ ] I swept the entire page is ticked
  • [ ] Validate page reports no blockers, and every warning was read
  • [ ] The draft is saved before Publish page

The hide-boxes sweep is the step that finds real errors. With the boxes drawn, the eye fills in what it expects; with them hidden, a missed paragraph is obvious.

→ Block Annotation§5.1 · Block Classes§5.3 · Block Boundaries§5.2 · Reading Order§5.9
